findings.title: ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary local path or URL via URLClassLoader
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } ); ... c = cl.loadClass( this.getClassname() ); ... return c.newInstance();
findings.entry_point: None in this variant. Constructor takes (path, classname); in applet mode (ApoConstants.B_APPLET==true) any URL string is accepted (line 68), otherwise a local filesystem path (line 66). Grep over all 60 files shows zero instantiations of ApoClassLoader.
findings.sink: Class.forName-equivalent loadClass() + c.newInstance() executing the loaded class's no-arg constructor (lines 73-75)
findings.data_path: getMyClass() -> new URL/File(path) -> URLClassLoader -> loadClass(classname) -> newInstance(). No caller exists between any input source and this chain in ApoMarc.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this variant: if a sibling variant wires this to a downloaded 'level plugin' or a level-server URL, an attacker hosting that URL serves a .class whose constructor runs arbitrary code on first instantiation. In ApoMarc itself nothing reaches it; an attacker would have to modify the JAR or add their own caller, at which point they already control the JVM.
findings.preconditions: Some code must construct ApoClassLoader with an attacker-controlled path/classname. In this variant none does (verified by grep for 'ApoClassLoader' across all sources).
findings.validation_plan: Confirm orphan status: `grep -rn "new ApoClassLoader" apoMarc org` returns nothing. Then prove the primitive works: compile a class Malicious { public Malicious(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("touch /tmp/pwn");} }, run `new ApoClassLoader("file:///tmp", "Malicious").getMyClass()` in a test harness and observe /tmp/pwn created - demonstrating that any future caller hands it RCE.

findings.title: Highscore submit/fetch over plain HTTP to apo-games.de with unauthenticated, fully forgeable scores
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php";
public final static String HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: ApoHighscore.save()/load() (org/apogames/help/ApoHighscore.java:63 and :109) open these URLs when ApoConstants.B_ONLINE==true (default true, ApoConstants.java:16). However, grep shows ApoHighscore has NO callers anywhere in the ApoMarc variant - the feature is orphaned here.
findings.sink: urlConn.getOutputStream() writes 'level=..&points=..&name=..' plaintext POST (ApoHighscore.java:72-77); urlConn.getInputStream() reads server-controlled response (ApoHighscore.java:81, 126)
findings.data_path: (if wired) game-over logic -> ApoHighscore.getInstance().save(level,solution,name) -> URL(HIGHSCORE_SAVEPHP).openConnection() -> DataOutputStream.writeBytes(content) over HTTP
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this variant; real in siblings that call it. (a) Network attacker/MITM reads the player's chosen name and modifies the response of load(), injecting arbitrary scoreboard names rendered in-game. (b) Local cheat: `curl -d 'level=99&points=999999&name=cheater' http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/save_highscore.php` submits a top score without playing - there is no signature, token, or session in the request (verified: content string at ApoHighscore.java:74-76 is the entire payload).
findings.preconditions: For network interception: the game must call ApoHighscore (it does not in ApoMarc) and the victim must play on a hostile network. For score forging: only access to the still-live endpoint. Note: domain may be defunct as of audit date.
findings.validation_plan: Orphan check: `grep -rn "ApoHighscore" --include=*.java . | grep -v help/ApoHighscore.java` returns nothing. Reachability of the flaw itself: run a traffic-capturing proxy (mitmproxy in transparent mode) or `tcpdump port 80`, temporarily invoke ApoHighscore.getInstance().save(7, 12345, "test") from a harness, observe the POST body in cleartext including name; replay the same POST via curl twice and see two identical entries accepted server-side (proves no nonce/integrity).

findings.title: Highscore loader trusts server response format; NumberFormatException from server data escapes handler
findings.entry_point: HTTP response body of http://www.apo-games.de/apoNotSoSimple/get_highscore.php, read line-by-line at ApoHighscore.java:129. Every third line must be an integer; names are taken verbatim.
findings.sink: Integer.valueOf(str) (lines 131, 133) inside load(); parsed values and raw name strings flow into the singleton's public lists getPoints()/getNames() consumed by UI rendering code
findings.data_path: malicious/compromised server (or MITM, since plain HTTP per ApoMarc-02) -> DataInputStream.readLine() -> i%3 dispatch -> Integer.valueOf / names.add -> ApoHighscore singleton lists
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this variant (load() never called). If wired: a hostile or hijacked server (or HTTP MITM) responds with 'abc' on a points line; Integer.valueOf throws NumberFormatException, which is NOT caught (only MalformedURLException and IOException are caught, lines 141-147), crashing the calling thread/game. Server also controls arbitrary strings displayed in the highscore UI.
findings.preconditions: B_ONLINE==true AND some game code calls load(); neither holds in ApoMarc (grep confirms zero callers).
findings.validation_plan: From a harness, point a local HTTP server returning three lines 'not_a_number\n1\nX' at the constant and call load(); observe uncaught NumberFormatException propagating out of load() despite its try/catch - demonstrating the parser gap. Orphan check: grep as in ApoMarc-02.

findings.title: AudioPlayer contains plain-HTTP music fetch branch from apo-games.de, currently dead (BInJAR hardwired true)
findings.entry_point: Would be the network: sound file fetched at runtime from http://www.apo-games.de/apoPongBeat<path> in applet mode. Dead code: field BInJAR is initialized true at line 19 ('private final boolean BInJAR = true;') so the branch is unreachable, and the game constructs AudioPlayer only via org/apogames/sound/ApoSounds.playSound (resource-name strings).
findings.sink: AudioSystem.getAudioInputStream(URL) parsing a server-supplied audio stream fed line-by-line into SourceDataLine.write (lines 94-98)
findings.data_path: ApoSounds.playSound(name) -> new AudioPlayer(path, loop).start() -> run():64 if(BInJAR) getResource(path) [taken] else if B_APPLET -> HTTP fetch (skipped)
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical as written: were BInJAR flipped to false in a sibling variant running as applet, a MITM on the plain-HTTP connection substitutes an audio file; worst realistic case is malformed-input parser bugs in javax.sound (historically exploitable) plus trivially blockable playback. As shipped, no untrusted bytes reach AudioSystem at all.
findings.preconditions: BInJAR changed to false AND applet mode AND hostile network position.
findings.validation_plan: Verify deadness: `javap -c` or read line 19 showing 'final boolean BInJAR = true', and confirm the else-branch at lines 66-71 cannot execute. To prove the latent path, reflectively/set BInJAR=false, run in applet mode behind mitmproxy, serve garbage on the requested URL, and observe exceptions from AudioSystem.getAudioInputStream - confirming server-controlled bytes enter javax.sound.

findings.title: ApoIO base class performs raw HTTP GET/POST level transfer in applet mode; no subclass in this variant
findings.code_excerpt:
URL connection = new URL(fileName);
data = new DataInputStream(connection.openStream());
findings.entry_point: readLevel(String)/readLevel(boolean bURL,...): when bURL==true (applet mode passes ApoConstants.B_APPLET, line 68) any fileName string is opened as URL; writeLevel(String) likewise POSTs to an arbitrary URL (lines 40-43). In this variant ZERO classes extend ApoIO (grep for 'extends ApoIO' finds none), so readLevel(DataInputStream)/writeLevel(DataOutputStream) bodies are empty abstractions.
findings.sink: connection.openStream() pulling untrusted bytes into the abstract hand-written parser readLevel(DataInputStream) implemented by subclasses (none here); writeLevel POSTing game data over HttpURLConnection (line 41)
findings.data_path: (in siblings) level-server download -> readLevel(bURL=true, url) -> openStream -> DataInputStream -> subclass's byte-level parse loop. In ApoMarc the chain terminates at the abstract method.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical here. This is exactly the infrastructure behind the corpus-wide '.mar/.skunk/get_level.php' pattern: in variants that subclass ApoIo, a malicious level server or HTTP MITM supplies truncated/hostile streams to hand-rolled parsers with no length/format validation. In ApoMarc no such parser exists, so there is nothing to attack.
findings.preconditions: A subclass implementing readLevel(DataInputStream) and a caller passing bURL=true with an attacker-chosen URL; neither exists in this variant.
findings.validation_plan: Orphan proof: `grep -rn "extends ApoIO" --include=*.java .` returns zero hits; instantiate an anonymous ApoIo in a harness and call readLevel(true,"http://127.0.0.1:8000/x") against netcat serving junk to confirm the transport opens before any parse - establishing that safety depends entirely on absent subclasses.

findings.title: MD5 helper present in shared library but never invoked (orphaned weak-hash capability)
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: grep across all 60 files shows getMd5Digest has zero call sites. It is presumably used for highscore/validation checksums in sibling variants.
findings.sink: MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") producing a collision-susceptible digest formatted as hex (lines 277-280)
findings.data_path: caller-provided string -> getMd5Digest -> MD5 -> 32-char uppercase hex returned. No data flows into it in ApoMarc.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical: in variants that validate levels/highscores with this function, MD5 collisions allow crafting substitute artifacts with matching checksums. In ApoMarc the function is inert, so no attacker action applies.
findings.preconditions: A caller would need to exist; it does not in this variant (also note pInput.getBytes() uses platform default charset, a correctness wart for any future caller).
findings.validation_plan: Run `grep -rn "getMd5Digest" --include=*.java .` - single hit at the definition. Cross-check sibling variants for callers to confirm the shared-component propagation hypothesis.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream/readObject anywhere in the variant (grep over all 60 files)
path_traversal - no user.home usage; the only user.dir use (AudioPlayer.java:70) sits in the same dead !BInJAR branch and builds a fixed resource path; game code touches no files
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, or keys embedded in sources
resource_exhaustion - no unbounded loops/allocations driven by external input in active code paths
custom save/level/replay parsing (.cheat/.mar/.rep/.skunk/.defence) - not present in this variant; ApoIO abstraction exists but has no concrete parser
notes: Directory layout quirk: under the stated source root the actual tree is nested one level deeper at 'Users/eliahilse/Documents/GitHub/B/apogames/Java/ApoMarc/'; all finding paths above are relative to that inner project root. Headline result: ApoMarc is the cleanest kind of variant for this study - its game-specific package (apoMarc/, incl. ApoMarcMain.main which ignores argv entirely, and ApoMarcApplet) performs zero file and zero network I/O; all images/audio come from JAR resources via ClassLoader.getResource. Every corpus-typical weakness (URLClassLoader code loading, plain-HTTP highscore, HTTP level I/O, MD5) survives only as ORPHANED cloned library code in org.apogames with no call sites, which is why every finding above is marked reachable=false. Security-relevant mutability worth flagging for cross-variant work: ApoConstants.B_APPLET/B_ONLINE are public static NON-final booleans (ApoConstants.java:12,16) flipped at runtime by the applet constructor (ApoMarcApplet.java:21) and ApoScreen.initApplet (ApoScreen.java:159); these flags silently switch file->network behavior in ApoIO/ApoImage/AudioPlayer, meaning a variant's reachability profile can change purely through its entry-point class. ApoImage.getImage also has a latent ImageIO.read(new URL(pic)) branch (ApoImage.java:89) gated on B_APPLET and bLoad=true, but every call site in this variant passes bLoad=false (e.g. ApoMarcPanel.java:55), so it was not counted as a separate finding.
